blocking_defects: GW mislabel: the claim-bearing "Giacomini-White" gate is implemented only as the scalar unconditional Diebold-Mariano special case (test function h_t == 1). k1709.py:1039-1091 builds a scalar loss differential, tests its mean with a Bartlett HAC standard error against a normal z, and never forms an instrument h_t, the vector moment h_t*dL_t, a q x q covariance, a Wald statistic, or a chi-square_q reference distribution. The reader-facing "GW gate / GW z / Giacomini-White on QLIKE" terminology (README.md:30-38, README.md:69-82) therefore overstates the test: it cannot support a conditional / state-dependent predictive-ability claim and could miss offsetting gains and losses across regimes. Codex notes the numeric p-values remain defensible for the weaker claim GW (2006) Sec. 3.4 actually licenses -- equal *unconditional* predictive ability under a bounded-memory forecasting method (where the GW statistic coincides with DM) -- so the defect is one of labelling and claim scope, not of arithmetic.

independent_findings.gw_vs_dm: BLOCKING -- see blocking_defects[0]. Rolling re-estimation (250-obs fixed-length window, k1709.py:949-998) is NOT a defect: GW bounded-memory asymptotics permit it. HAC/Newey-West bandwidth (~n^(1/3), o(n), > h-1) is appropriate for the loss differential actually tested.
independent_findings.lookahead_and_seeding: NO BLOCKING DEFECT -- no claim-bearing look-ahead found (predictors lagged via state_lag/flow_lag, flow scaling uses only prior 20 days, OOS training labels close strictly before the forecast origin, shock thresholds are fixed literals, no randomized split). All stochastic procedures seeded (global seed, bootstrap RNG + per-cell seed, per-beta power RNG).

non_blocking_observations: qlike_gain_upper_bound assumes z(m) is globally increasing; 4 primary streams are mildly non-monotone. Dense checks found exactly one crossing at both pointwise and Bonferroni critical values, so every frozen bound remains valid, but the inversion should verify the full rejection set rather than assume monotonicity.
Figure 2 treats an already-lagged flow regressor as event day zero, shifting the displayed flow-shock date one day forward (k1709.py:2530-2555). Does not feed inference.
